Subject: APAC/EU/US phased capacity ramp and onboarding checklist for Pavo Analytics

Hi Maria / Pavo ops team,

Thanks for the kickoff call today — good to align on scope. As discussed, I sketched a phased capacity proposal that ties to your expected launch bursts and deal milestones. Key asks from our side to accelerate a smooth Dedicated onboarding: 

- Confirm expected peak TPS (requests/min) per region during launch week (US/EU/APAC) and steady-state Q1.
- Share token/response-size distribution (short chat vs long generation) — helps pick quantization/batch profiles.
- Any compliance constraints for EU data residency or APAC cloud provider preferences.

I attached a quick compute profile spreadsheet (pavo_compute_profile_v1.xlsx) and a mock SOW template we can iterate on. If you can get the numbers by Wednesday EOD PST, we can lock a tri-region boot allocation and map tranche triggers to your billing milestones.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Pavo: populate compute_profile sheet by 2027-09-22 EOD
2) Redwood (Laura + Karthik): return an initial tranche plan + SOW redline by 2027-09-24
3) Ops sync (optional): 30-min follow-up Thurs to review burst profiles

Thanks — will loop Hannah for scheduling the follow-up.

Best,
David Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi David — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. Quick answers from our side: 

- Peak TPS: US 280 req/min, EU 120 req/min, APAC 90 req/min during the 2-week launch window. Steady-state estimate: US 70, EU 30, APAC 25.
- Token profile: ~85% short chat (<=256 tokens), 15% long generation (avg 1200 tokens).
- Residency: EU data must remain in EU for EU-only endpoints. APAC: open to either SG or JP (preference SG).

We filled a first pass into pavo_compute_profile_v1.xlsx — attached. One follow-up: can Redwood provide a recommended buffer multiplier for the first month (we expect unpredictable spikes)?

Cheers,
Maria Lopez
Head of Ops, Pavo Analytics

David / team — thanks Maria for the filled sheet. I reviewed the numbers quickly. High-level notes: 

- We should size initial dedicated pools with a 2.5x buffer on peak to keep latency SLOs during bursty traffic and to accommodate KV cache warmup. That matches recent tri-region pilots.
- Suggested initial allocation (GPU-equivalent slots) by region: US: 18 slots, EU: 8 slots (Frankfurt), APAC: 6 slots (Singapore).
- Suggested startup quantization profile: US/EU use int8-quant for majority workload; APAC pilot can start int8 but we keep a small fp16 headroom for long generations.

I'll produce a tranche-trigger table linking committed spend milestones to automatic node add/remove (canary triggers + 72-hour notice windows) and draft a minimal SOW redline. David — please attach your mock SOW and the timeline CSV so I can align the legal/config language.

Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
